notes: C7 hardening (protocol amage.verified-deploy/2) on the same C7 lineage: C7 = C6 r2parts (c6Reference) + verified-deploy gate (patchCommit, crates only: keybroker Ed25519 helper via aws_lc_rs, local_backend/src/bendvex.rs, start_push/finish_push/evaluate_*/push_config gates, source package SHA-256) + the two provenance labels in self-hosted/docker-build/Dockerfile.backend (org.amage.patch-commit, org.amage.verified-deploy.protocol). cliCommit adds the CLI half (npm-packages/convex/src/cli/lib/verifiedDeploy.ts); it is outside patchPaths and does not enter the runtime image. Protected mode is opt-in per process: AMAGE_VERIFIED_DEPLOY_PUBKEY=<hex64>[@notAfter][,<hex64>[@notAfter]...] (the trust set; kid = sha256 of the raw key) and AMAGE_VERIFIED_DEPLOY_SUPERVISOR_URL=<origin> (required: the backend asks the supervisor online at start_push and finish_push). The supervisor's install receipt, sent as the adminKey token, is the only deploy credential; it is an admin identity limited to DeploymentOp::Deploy. No key, credential or policy is baked into the image. patchSha256 is the harness command (self-hosted/test-candidate.mjs, base vs working tree): git diff --binary --no-ext-diff --no-color --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ --abbrev=9 849a6fc605b5a910c9834b61a77c5475cc24d189 -- crates Cargo.toml Cargo.lock self-hosted/docker-build rust-toolchain .cargo | sha256sum. The image label org.amage.patch-sha256 and the version string carry that value. patchSha256MnemonicPrefixes is the same diff with --src-prefix=c/ --dst-prefix=i/ (the command written in AMAGE.md for C6, which came from git diff.mnemonicPrefix=true): the original C6 hash 6a1de1f6 reproduces only with c/ i/, while the published C6 r2parts hash 910724b4 reproduces only with a/ b/ (its patchPrefixes field is stale). C7 records both and puts the harness-verifiable one in the image. patchCommit is the gate commit; the Dockerfile label change was made on top of cliCommit and is part of the hashed patch, so git diff base patchCommit alone does not reproduce patchSha256 — the working tree (or the commit that lands the Dockerfile change) does. imageId is docker's .Id, which on the build host (containerd image store) is the OCI index digest covering the linux/amd64 manifest (amd64ManifestDigest) plus a buildx provenance attestation; configDigest is the content-addressed image config, the identity that survives push/pull (docker pull by digest must report it again). builtAt is the image config's created time. buildSourceTree/headCommit/buildTreeDirty record exactly what was built; a rebuild is not byte-reproducible (APT/runtime inputs float), so imageId identifies the artifact actually tested. image is a LOCAL tag only. No registry digest exists until a push, which is out of scope for this manifest; the future name would be ghcr.io/amageweb/convex-backend:<version-with-'+base…' replaced by '-<patchSha12>'> pinned by digestReference, as in amage-candidate6-r2parts.json.
